source_fields.objective: min_{x in X} Phi(x), Phi(x)=max_{y in Y}f(x,y)+indicator_X(x)

assumptions.scope: The complete stated domain. Constants remain uniform when the other variable block is fixed.
assumptions.description: The set $X$ is known, nonempty, closed, and convex. The set $Y$ is known, nonempty, compact, and convex, with $\operatorname{diam}(Y)\le D_y$.

assumptions.scope: The complete stated domain. Constants remain uniform when the other variable block is fixed.
assumptions.description: The function $f$ is jointly $\beta$-smooth on $X\times Y$. For every $x$, $f(x,\cdot)$ is concave. Convexity in the $x$ direction and a positive strong-concavity modulus are not required.

assumptions.scope: The complete stated domain. Constants remain uniform when the other variable block is fixed.
assumptions.description: The public feasible initial point $(x_0,y_0)$ satisfies $\Phi(x_0)-\inf_{x\in X}\Phi(x)\le\Delta<\infty$, where $\Phi(x)=\max_{y\in Y}f(x,y)$.

source_fields.parameter_domain_description: $D_y$: nonnegative real; $\Delta$: positive real; $\beta$: positive real; $d$: integer at least 2; $\varepsilon$: positive real. Derived quantities are defined in the parameter table. Each region states any additional accuracy and dimension conditions.

source_fields.geometry: known domains with exact projections; geometry cost retained separately

operations.order_convention: Derivative order refers to the scalar payoff $f$. The joint gradient has two blocks; the response signature specifies whether a Hessian or complete derivative jet is supplied.

feedback_quality.description: Exact responses from the same hidden object fixed before interaction

operations.coupling: The exact response map is fixed before interaction; repeated calls are charged separately.

operations.order_convention: This operation is charged according to its explicit input and output, not renamed according to a scalar function's derivative order.

source_fields.postprocessing: arbitrary measurable transcript-based output unless algorithm restriction expressly states otherwise
source_fields.feasibility: Return a feasible pair $(\widehat x,\widehat y)\in X\times Y$.
source_fields.allowed_postprocessing: The output may be any measurable postprocessing of the history, including an unqueried point, average, or convex combination. It must satisfy the stated domain and feasibility requirements; no additional function value or computable certificate is required.
source_fields.certificate_requirement: No additional computable certificate is required beyond any graph element explicitly listed in the output.

source_fields.normalization: The exact formula governs; norms, squares, maxima, and expectations are not interchanged.
source_fields.finiteness_conditions: Use the compact-domain, solution-existence, and smoothness assumptions in the model and the stated metric definition.
